fullPassage: In today's marketing and advertising-soaked world, people cannot escape brands. The younger they are when they start using a brand or product, the more likely they are to keep using it for years to come. But that's not the only reason companies are aiming their marketing and advertising at younger consumers. As James U. McNeal, a professor at Texas A&M University, puts it, "Seventy-five percent of spontaneous food purchases can be traced to a nagging child. And one out of two mothers will buy a food simply because her child requests it. To trigger desire in a child is to trigger desire in the whole family." In other words, kids have power over spending in their households, they have power over their grandparents and they have power over their babysitters. That's why companies use tricks to manipulate their minds.

questions.passage: In today's marketing and advertising-soaked world, people cannot escape brands. The younger they are when they start using a brand or product, the more likely they are to keep using it for years to come. But that's not the only reason companies are aiming their marketing and advertising at younger consumers. As James U. McNeal, a professor at Texas A&M University, puts it, "Seventy-five percent of spontaneous food purchases can be traced to a nagging child. And one out of two mothers will buy a food simply because her child requests it. To trigger desire in a child is to trigger desire in the whole family." In other words, kids have power over spending in their households, they have power over their grandparents and they have power over their babysitters. That's why companies use tricks to manipulate their minds.

det.korean: tricks(속임수): 기업들이 아이들의 마음을 조종하기 위해 속임수를 사용한다.
det.analysis: 원문 마지막 문장: companies use tricks to manipulate their minds. 기업이 아이들의 마음을 조종하기 위해 사용하는 수단 = tricks(속임수).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
